correctness.rationale: Legendre produces the exact valuation \(s_2(n)+c_1+c_2\) of every positive Strehl summand, where both c-values count binary carries and are nonnegative. Both vanish precisely when \(a=n-k\) selects adjacent-one positions in n. There are \(2^{t(n)}\) choices; reduction of the normalized sum mod 2 proves valuation equality exactly if \(t(n)=0\). Standard Fibonacci word counting and a binomial sparse-index bound prove the two corollaries. The standalone checker verifies every positive term through n=256 and does not substitute finite tests for the proof.

originality.rationale: The new classification concerns equality in an index-dependent valuation inequality, not merely the underlying Franel sum. Inspected 2011, 2014 and 2015 primary works establish the Strehl identity, odd-prime congruences, empirical valuation trees or mod-p Lucas properties, none of which states or directly implies the two-carry minimum-term census and parity characterization. An unindexed dominating theorem is a residual risk, not ruled out by unsuccessful searches.
residual_risks: A more general binomial-sum divisibility or 2-adic valuation theorem not indexed by these queries could cover the same parity characterization.

The complete sharpness set of the natural digit-sum lower bound, exact minimum-summand multiplicities, and Fibonacci count are infinite structural classifications useful even though the larger valuations are unknown.
